definition: Racter is an artificial intelligence program that generates English language prose at random.
details: It was published by Mindscape for IBM PC compatibles in 1984, then for the Apple II, Mac, and Amiga. An expanded version of the software, not the one released through Mindscape, was used to generate the text for the published book The Policeman's Beard Is Half Constructed.

explainer.lead: Racter was an early program that produced English prose at random, showing that machine-generated text could be published as a book. It marks one of the first commercial attempts to sell computer-authored writing to the public.

tiers.eli5: It is a computer program that strings English words together to make paragraphs, a bit like pulling random sentences out of a hat.
tiers.practitioner: It is a historical reference point for text generation, useful when explaining how far language models have come. A pitfall is treating its random output as meaningful composition.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as an AI program that generates English language prose at random; no formal model is specified. Its scope is limited to random prose generation rather than coherent or responsive writing.

explainer.example: The book The Policeman's Beard Is Half Constructed was generated using an expanded version of the software rather than the Mindscape release.
